clue.text: One tearing into extremely fruity trifles?

indicators.note: into signals the ripper going inside the outer letters
extremely means at the extremes, so only the outermost letters of fruity are used

parts.note: a ripper is one who tears or rips things

explanation.surface: Someone tucking greedily into a very fruity trifle pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifles' looks like the British pudding, but here it means worthless knick-knacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, unnecessary ornaments and trinkets are trifles in the sense of things of little value.

clue.text: Provide new community for theatre the Spanish writer set up

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

explanation.surface: A Spanish playwright establishes a theatre to give a town new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns ELPOE round to EOPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill a place again with inhabitants is to give it a fresh population.

clue.text: Protestant, before initially singing some bits, rushed to invite one in

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of singing

parts.note: a byte is a group of computer bits, usually eight

indicators.note: to invite, with in, means asking someone to come inside, so one goes into rushed
in completes the phrase 'invite one in', placing one inside

parts.note: ran means rushed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A churchgoer sang a few snatches before hurrying to let someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Church of Scotland and similar churches are a Protestant denomination.

clue.text: Unusually apt clue covering Yankee oil producer

indicators.note: covering means going over, so the shuffled letters surround the Yankee
unusually signals the letters appearing in an unusual order

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cryptic clue about an American oilman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' anagrams APT CLUE to EUCALPT; 'covering' puts it round Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum trees yield eucalyptus oil, so the tree is literally an oil producer.

clue.text: Turn up with husband in tent, supplying healthy food

indicators.note: in puts the reversed turn and husband inside the tent

parts.note: a yurt is a round Mongolian tent

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Arriving at a campsite with your partner, bringing wholesome snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the word for a turn from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultured dairy product often marketed as good for the gut is a healthy food.

clue.text: Graduate at Sorbonne who at first supported French underground

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
the Sorbonne is a Paris university, so who in French is qui

indicators.note: at first picks the first letter of supported

explanation.surface: A Paris graduate who backed the French Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name for the French Resistance fighters of the Second World War, an underground movement.

clue.text: Characters entering for a Latin exam

indicators.note: characters entering means letters found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Students putting themselves forward for a Latin examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as opposed to a written paper, is a type of exam.

clue.text: Not the condition of drunkard unknown to eat cheese?

definitions.text: Not the condition of drunkard unknown to eat cheese?

indicators.note: to eat means taking something inside, so the drunkard's letters enclose the cheese

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Brie is a soft French cheese
in algebra unknowns are x, y and z, so y stands for an unknown

explanation.surface: A tipsy man who doesn't know to eat cheese isn't in a sober state.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while 'drunkard unknown to eat cheese' builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of not being drunk is the opposite of a drunkard's condition.

clue.text: Work with men at old port

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian port, is often just Rio

explanation.surface: A work party of men toiling at an old harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition is a work, and a large sacred choral piece is one such kind.

clue.text: Church feature identified in downloads, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word for downloads is to be said out loud

parts.note: apps are programs you download to a phone

explanation.surface: Something about a church spotted among files on a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church is a typical architectural feature.

clue.text: Swaggering adventurer's sister about to clean clasp

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link to the rest; the definition is the swaggering adventurer

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sister's letters surround the rest

parts.note: to wash is to clean
a buckle is a clasp on a belt or shoe

explanation.surface: A dashing hero's sister is busy polishing a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring, flamboyant pirate or sword-fighting hero is the classic swaggering adventurer.

clue.text: Be perfectly aware what's short of water, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear asks whether this sounds like the phrase, signalling something spoken

parts.note: a well short of water could be described as no full well

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a dry well.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be fully conscious of something, often while pretending otherwise.

clue.text: Agent crossing railway line nimbly

indicators.note: crossing means the agent's letters go across, spanning the others

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A spy darting nimbly across a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in an agile, lively way is moving nimbly.

clue.text: Reformed persons finally make comeback

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so these letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of make

explanation.surface: Former offenders, having changed their ways, make a return to society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' anagrams PERSONS to RESPONS; 'finally' adds E from make.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeback is a retort or reply, which is what a response is.

clue.text: Inferior to some quarters in spa city

indicators.note: in puts the compass points inside the city

parts.note: Bath is an English city famous for its Roman spa
quarters are compass points; east-north-east is formed from some of them

explanation.surface: Certain districts of a spa town are considered second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lower in rank or status than something is being below it.

clue.text: Uproar when brown bear traps leaders of large youth hostel

indicators.note: traps means holds inside, so the bear's letters enclose the initials

parts.note: Baloo is the brown bear in Kipling's The Jungle Book

indicators.note: leaders of picks the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: Chaos when a bear corners the head of a youth hostel.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or fuss is an uproar.

clue.text: Words maybe associated with some fine gauzy fabric

parts.note: having words is quarrelling, so words can be a tiff
any can mean some, as in 'have you any milk'

explanation.surface: Vocabulary linked to a delicate, sheer material.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a thin, transparent muslin-like cloth, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: This writer's books about store, due out soon

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces surround the store

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, so this writer's is I'm
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
a mine is a store, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: An author's books are shortly to arrive in the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen or be released very soon is on the point of occurring.

clue.text: Curious thing about soft drink at bedtime

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about
p is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: An odd item regarding a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink, often alcoholic, taken just before going to sleep has this name.

clue.text: Time a girl embraces popular sovereign's wife

indicators.note: embraces means holds inside, so the girl's letters enclose popular

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: For a while a girl hugs a well-liked queen consort.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor was a tsar, and his wife held this title as empress.

clue.text: Sloth unknown in East, captured by young woman

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the young woman's letters

parts.note: a lass is a young woman
in algebra unknowns are x, y and z, so z stands for an unknown

explanation.surface: A sloth from an unknown eastern land caught by a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the animal, but it is the deadly sin of idleness. ZINE goes inside LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth as one of the seven deadly sins is idleness, an unwillingness to work.

clue.text: English knight competed, being grudgingly admired

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
vied means competed

explanation.surface: An English knight who took part in a tournament earned reluctant respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Coveting someone's qualities while resenting them is admiring with grudge.

clue.text: Old lady sheltering a convict in Continental resort

indicators.note: sheltering means keeping the other letters inside

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, MA
an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: Mother hiding an escaped prisoner at a European holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This Spanish city on the Costa del Sol is a popular holiday destination on the European mainland.

clue.text: Our new envoy foolishly crosses king — anything could happen!

indicators.note: crosses means spans, so the shuffled letters go either side of the king
foolishly means arranged in a silly way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A diplomat foolishly offends a monarch, with unpredictable consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' anagrams OUR NEW ENVOY to YOUNEVER NOW, which 'crosses' K.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a saying used to stress that the future is unpredictable.

clue.text: One who employs asses regularly in ancient city

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the ancient city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of asses

explanation.surface: Someone using donkeys in an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes use of something is one who employs it.

clue.text: Make an impression, and so on, with Head of History

parts.note: etc. is short for et cetera, meaning and so on

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of History

explanation.surface: A history teacher trying to make their mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave lines into metal or glass is to cut an impression into a surface.

clue.text: Supervised old archdeacon, suppressing language

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the archdeacon's letters enclose the language

parts.note: an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
Erse is Scottish or Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: An elderly clergyman kept tight control by silencing a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Having watched over and directed work means having supervised it.

clue.text: Bovid mammal bound to be tied to stake

indicators.note: to be tied to stake puts the bound after the stake, attached behind it

parts.note: an ante is a stake put up in poker
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: An animal that is bound to end up tethered to a post.
explanation.definitionFit: This horned, deer-like grazer belongs to the bovid family alongside cattle and goats.
